articles.title: Can I get too much protein? Experts answer your questions on the popular supplement
articles.summary: If you’re wondering whether ‘organic’ really matters or if there’s such a thing as too much protein, this is for you. The 10 best (and worst) whey protein powders – tested. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: If our protein powder taste test taught us anything, it’s that these supplements are confusing.
While plant and whey powders are both popular, we opted for whey, given its surging prices and popularity (and the former’s higher risk of lead ).
What started as a simple mission to find the best-tasting powders soon led us down a rabbit hole, asking, “What does NSF certification mean?” and “Is organic whey actually better?”

To further muddy the waters, the US Food and Drug Administration doesn’t test the safety of protein powders, including whether they contain heavy metals such as lead. They also don’t verify marketing claims promising improved muscle growth or recovery.

articles.title: Autumn is here, and I’ve got five micro-moments of joy to see us through
articles.summary: For those of us who don’t like the chilly seasons, ‘glimmers’ are the way to go. This year mine are woolly, furry, scaly and crunchy. It finally got cold and dark in my neighbourhood last week.
body: It’s time to find some “glimmers”, which is what we’re calling little fragments of cheer now. “Micro moments of happiness that can flip the script on your day” have gone “pretty mainstream”, Grazia magazine said last month, but if you missed the memo, me too. I was busy spiralling into heatwave-fuelled existential dread when trend forecasters explored the glimmer concept this spring – it’s been a low-glimmer time for me.

Grazia’s glimmers included a perfume actually called Glimmer and gel masks that make you look like a ghoul, but for anyone sinking deep into seasonal affective disorder, sheet masks won’t cut it. So I set myself the challenge of suggesting five glimmers I hope are (almost) universally cheering.
First, unearthing pictures of Lenny Kravitz’s massive scarf. The man wears a full flock of sheep round his neck in winter like it’s nothing – how delightful.
Second, who could fail to be thrilled by bluefin tuna returning to UK waters? They can weigh as much as a grand piano – imagine thousands of scaly Steinways hanging out around Whitby!

articles.title: The one change that worked: numb with grief, I sat in the dark, surrounded by strangers – and began to heal
articles.summary: Life had come crashing to a halt when I lost my brother. But in the cinema I found comfort and a strange solidarity. In 2022, my younger brother drowned in an accident. His death reset life as I knew it. I had been offered my first proper job; I didn’t take it.
body: At home, there were now three of us. We orbited separate corners of the house, each needing a different thing for comfort: for my mum, exercise; for my dad, music; for me, escape.

It was a long, grey January, and I was stuck in the mud. My brain had puffed up like an airbag against the full force of grief; my head was fuzzy and foggy, my thoughts were sludge. I was so sensitive to light and sound that it felt as if a layer of my skin had been peeled off. Mostly, though, I just felt nothing.

I was in limbo. In my early 20s, I couldn’t haunt the house indefinitely. At some point, I would need to rejoin the land of the living. But for now, stepping back on to the hamster wheel felt pointless.

Getting out of the house, at least, I could manage. But where to go? I had seen a sign at my local cinema for an under-25s membership, which offered weekday tickets for £5.99. It would be a relief, I thought, to lose myself in a fantastical world for a few hours. So I pulled on my dad’s coat, made a flask of tea and took a blustery walk down the hill to Greenwich.
points: Life had come crashing to a halt when I lost my brother.
But in the cinema I found comfort and a strange solidarity.

I had been offered my first proper job; I didn’t take it.

articles.title: Vive Le Ballet! Matthieu Blazy’s Chanel Lights Up the Stage at the Opéra Garnier
articles.summary: On Saturday night, le Tout-Paris gathered at the Opéra Garnier for the opening gala of the ballet season. The evening started by honoring tradition with a défilé set to Berlioz’s Marche des Troyens.
body: The procession featured the entire company—the ballerinas all in tutus and diadems by Chanel—from eight-year-old petits rats to étoiles including the newly appointed Thomas Docquir, Hugo Marchand, Germain Louvet, Guillaume Diop, Hannah O’Neill, Léonore Baulac, and Dorothée Gilbert, who will give her farewell performance this Thursday.

Gilbert’s was not the only imminent farewell: come July, the Opéra Garnier itself will be shuttered for an extensive five-year renovation estimated at some €450 million. In the interim, the ballet will perform at the Opéra Bastille. Chanel, the Opéra Garnier’s Major Patron and Exceptional Patron for the renovation, was joined by Rolex, Timepiece of the Paris Opéra, as lead sponsors of the evening, which raised €1.8 million toward the works.

articles.title: The Oldest Covered Food Market in Paris, Marché des Enfants Rouges, Is Destroyed in Fire
articles.summary: An overnight blaze has destroyed the historic Marché des Enfants Rouges in the Marais, one of the French capital's most beloved food destinations.
body: One of Paris 's most iconic food markets has been devastated by a fire that broke out in the early hours of Monday, October 12, causing extensive damage to a historic landmark that has been at the heart of the city's food scene for more than 400 years.
The Marché des Enfants Rouges, tucked away on Rue de Bretagne in the fashionable Marais neighborhood, is the oldest covered food market in Paris and a favorite among locals and visitors alike.

According to Le Monde, around 150 firefighters and 50 emergency vehicles were deployed to tackle the blaze, which engulfed the market overnight. Lieutenant-Colonel Pierre de Bouvier of the Paris fire brigade described the covered market as “completely destroyed,” although firefighters managed to prevent the flames from spreading to neighboring buildings. No serious injuries have been reported. The cause of the fire remains unknown and an investigation has been launched.
points: An overnight blaze has destroyed the historic Marché des Enfants Rouges in the Marais, one of the French capital's most beloved food destinations.

articles.title: Daisy Edgar-Jones Hops on the Graphic Tee Trend With a Vintage Deep Cut
articles.summary: Daisy Edgar-Jones isn’t joining the throngs of celebrities in a “Spoiled Boys” tee or bootleg Knicks merch. Instead, she turned to Stella McCartney’s Chloé.
body: Daisy Edgar-Jones sees your trendy graphic tee craze and raises you a vintage deep cut.

The actor swapped her thematically appropriate Sense and Sensibility press tour style for something a little more contemporary today in New York, trading in her corseted dresses and Napoleon jackets for a pair of au courant graphic T-shirts. But Edgar-Jones isn’t joining the throngs of celebrities in Emily Dawn Long’s “Spoiled Boys” tee or bootleg Knicks merch. Instead, she and stylist Dani Michelle turned to Stella McCartney-era Chloé.

Today, the actor wore two of McCartney’s airbrushed bird shirts from her spring 1999 collection for Chloé (fun fact: friend Phoebe Philo was designing there under her). For her first look of the day, Edgar-Jones opted for a white fitted shirt with three-quarter-length sleeves, a hummingbird sucking nectar from a flower emblazoned on her chest. She paired the sweet tee with a pair of chartreuse-yellow leather Jean Paul Gaultier pants and strappy silver heels.
points: Daisy Edgar-Jones isn’t joining the throngs of celebrities in a “Spoiled Boys” tee or bootleg Knicks merch.

articles.title: The 38 Best Restaurants in Rome, According to a Best-Selling Local Cookbook Author
articles.summary: Roman cuisine is a reflection of the city itself — layered, deeply rooted in tradition, and full of contrasts. After years of eating my way through Rome, I’ve found the best meals are shaped as much by history as the hands that prepare them.
body: Rome in February and March can feel like a damp intermission which pivots quickly toward spring. One day you’re ducking into bars to escape the downpour and the next you’re scanning patios for a table in the sun. If recent years are any indication, high season now revs up well before Holy Week, and by late March the city is already moving at full tilt. This is the narrow stretch to lean into artichokes simmered with the first peas, favas, and lettuce into vignarola, Rome’s definitive spring stew. Blink and you’ll miss it.

Eating and drinking well in Rome isn’t just about knowing where to go; it’s about knowing how to navigate the city’s idiosyncratic dining culture. Travelers often book tables months in advance, making last-minute reservations tough. While online booking is becoming more common, many places still rely on the phone, and it’s best to call at the very start or very end of service, when the staff actually has time to pick up. Plan ahead — but leave some room for spontaneity too.
points: Roman cuisine is a reflection of the city itself — layered, deeply rooted in tradition, and full of contrasts.

articles.title: The New Front Row: Who’s Who at New York, London, Milan, and Paris Fashion Week
articles.summary: Vogue photographed 35 shows across fashion month to find out who’s sitting front row, from celebrities to influencers—and where they’re seated.
body: Put aside the fact that the pool of applicants is self-selecting, then hand-plucked a few times over; the average person is significantly more likely to be struck by lightning than to sit front row at Paris Fashion Week in any given year. The front row is fashion’s premier place for mingling and status signaling. For as long as it has existed, it has reflected the culture, tracking technological, social, and structural change in 35mm, DSLR, and iPhone.

In the past century, it has transformed from an intimate gathering place for clientele into the manifestation of a growing industry, stuffed with a thickening horde of photographers, buyers, and press. As supermodels put fashion at the center of popular culture, celebrities joined their ranks. When the internet cracked the whole thing open, first came the bloggers and then came the influencers. If all the prior eras of the front row were defined by the appearance of a new group, today’s front row will be remembered for the presence—in equal and escalating measure—of all of the above (and more) at once.
All eyes used to be in the front row. Now all eyes are on it.

articles.title: Use This Hack to Get the Pixel's AI Dictation on Any Android Phone
articles.summary: Rambler, Google's AI-powered dictation feature, seems genuinely useful. At its core, Rambler is like your phone's existing dictation tool, only much smarter. It can automatically edit your speech into a more polished end product.
body: This is the type of feature most of us would like to have on our phones, there's only one problem: Despite developing the Android operating system, Google decided to make Rambler a Pixel 11-exclusive feature. As such, if you have a non-Pixel phone, like a Samsung or a Motorola, you're out of luck, unless you want to upgrade to one of Google's smartphones—or, as it turns out, download this third-party tool instead.

As reported by Android Authority, developer Akshay Kadam modded Google's Gboard app and uploaded it to GitHub under the name PixelBoard. Kadam advertises PixelBoard as a "supercharged Gboard mod" sporting features from the Pixel 11 series—including AI writing tools, and, notably, Rambler.

According to Kadam's GitHub page, PixelBoard runs side-by-side with the Gboard app on your phone. You don't need to replace the existing app or uninstall it, nor do you need to root your Android. Still, this is an unofficial port that requires sideloading onto your Android device. While the tool comes from a public GitHub page, exercise caution if you want to give it a shot.
points: Rambler, Google's AI-powered dictation feature, seems genuinely useful.

articles.title: How to Try WhatsApp's New Scheduled Messages Feature Early
articles.summary: All messaging apps should let you schedule texts by default. Sometimes, you need to send a message to a friend or family member, but you don't want them to get it just yet.
body: Of course, this is not a standard feature in all apps yet. Some apps have it, like Telegram or iMessage, and it's a great addition when you need it. Others, like Messenger or WhatsApp, are sorely missing it. While Meta doesn't appear to have any plans to bring scheduled texts to Messenger, it does seem like WhatsApp users are getting the upgrade on the horizon. In fact, you might be able to try it out today.

As reported by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is currently testing a new feature for users to schedule texts, photos, and videos to send at a later time. At this time, the feature works even when you're offline, so your scheduled messages will still send even if you don't have a wifi or cellular connection. In addition, the feature is not limited to single chats, as so many new messaging features are. You can schedule texts in both one-on-one and group chats, and all scheduled messages are still end-to-end encrypted.

articles.title: Chef Daniel Humm Dreams of a Restaurant Where No One Wants to Leave
articles.summary: The world-renowned chef reflects on the insanity and romance of opening his newest restaurant.
body: You spend years obsessing over details nobody should reasonably care about. You argue about chairs. You move light fixtures three inches. You hold entire meetings about a shade of red. Somehow, that bathroom doorknob is a matter of life and death.
You debate neighborhoods and foot traffic. You sign leases and personal guarantees that make you quiver. You sigh as construction budgets go over, knowing profit margins are always razor thin.

But somehow, you convince a group of people to believe in a vision that exists only in your head. Then one day you open the doors, inviting strangers to come in and decide its future. It’s insane, but it's exactly how things should be.

The truth is I love restaurants. I love running them. I love the thousand moving pieces that come together into something that feels alive. Restaurants are the place where those obsessions over details are useful.
